mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% over two consecutive months signals central bank policy over-tightening, which raises real discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% and remains > 0.3% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: accelerating inflation in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified inflation spike (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL reverts below 0.3% within one month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) accompanied by a parallel decline in UNRATE (labor force participation) indicates a tight labor market, which raises wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for three consecutive months while UNRATE decreases for three consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market tightness developing over multiple months
failure_condition: Rank IC for the combined (PAYEMS - UNRATE) signal < 0.05 over the 60-day horizon in more than 70% of triggered periods, or SPX 60-day returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly increase in HOUST (retail sales) exceeding 2% suggests strengthening consumer demand, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports equity price appreciation, yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 50% of 5-day windows with HOUST > +2% show non-positive 5-day forward returns (median negative), or the signal is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) below -1% indicates softening supply-side conditions, which raises uncertainty and compresses growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: More than 60% of INDPRO < -1% windows result in non-negative 20-day forward returns (median positive), or the effect is not statistically robust (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS for three consecutive months followed by a hold at the lower bound is interpreted as a policy pause, which reduces real rates and supports equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines for three consecutive months then remains flat for at least two months
regime_hint: policy pause after three months of rate cuts
failure_condition: Rank IC for the post-pause 60-day window is negative, or SPX 60-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in > 50% of such windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in UNRATE accompanied by a decline in PAYEMS signals labor market cooling, which increases uncertainty about wage growth and corporate hiring, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by > 0.2% month-over-month while PAYEMS decreases for two consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market cooling detected by dual series cross-pressure
failure_condition: More than 70% of triggered windows show non-negative 20-day returns despite the signal, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time monthly spike in GDPC1 (GDP momentum) above +5% suggests a burst in economic activity that is not yet reflected in earnings, creating optimism and pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 exceeds +5% in a single month
failure_condition: In more than 80% of such spikes, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the shock dissipates within one trading day.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in RSAFS (retail sales of final goods) of at least 4% indicates weakening demand for durable goods, which raises uncertainty and compresses growth prospects, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >= 4% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: prolonged weakness in durable goods demand
failure_condition: More than 60% of triggered windows with RSAFS decline show non-negative 20-day returns, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
